sentences.zh: 龐尚鵬宋儀望張嶽李材陸樹德蕭廩賈三近李頤朱鴻謨蕭彥

translations.literal: Pang Shangpeng, Song Yiwang, Zhang Yue, Li Cai, Lu Shude, Xiao Lin, Jia Sanjin, Li Yi, Zhu Hongmo, Xiao Yan
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shangpeng, Song Yiwang, Zhang Yue, Li Cai, Lu Shude, Xiao Lin, Jia Sanjin, Li Yi, Zhu Hongmo, and Xiao Yan

sentences.zh: 〈（弟雍查鐸）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brothers Yong, Cha, and Duo)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (See also Yong, Cha, and Duo)]〉

sentences.zh: 孫維城謝傑郭惟賢萬象春鐘化民吳達可

translations.literal: Sun Weicheng, Xie Jie, Guo Weixian, Wan Xiangchun, Zhong Huamin, Wu Dake
translations.idiomatic: Sun Weicheng, Xie Jie, Guo Weixian, Wan Xiangchun, Zhong Huamin, and Wu Dake

sentences.zh: 明年春，朝議興九邊屯、鹽。

translations.literal: The next spring, the court discussed promoting the nine frontier garrison colonies and salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, the court debated reviving garrison farming and salt policy along the nine frontier sectors.

sentences.zh: 擢尚鵬右僉都御史，與副都御史鄒應龍、唐繼祿分理。

translations.literal: Shangpeng was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zou Yinglong and Tang Jilu, divided the duties among them.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and shared the work with Vice Censors-in-Chief Zou Yinglong and Tang Jilu.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬轄兩淮、長蘆、山東三運司，兼理畿輔、河南、山東、江北、遼東屯務。

translations.literal: Shangpeng had jurisdiction over the three transport commissions of Liang-Huai, Changlu, and Shandong, and also oversaw garrison-colony affairs in the capital region, Henan, Shandong, Jiangbei, and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng oversaw the Liang-Huai, Changlu, and Shandong salt transport offices while also supervising garrison colonies in the capital districts, Henan, Shandong, Jiangbei, and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 抵昌平，劾內侍張恩擅殺人，兩淮巡鹽孫以仁贓罪，皆獲譴。

translations.literal: On reaching Changping, he impeached the eunuch Zhang En for killing people on his own authority and the Liang-Huai salt inspector Sun Yiren for corruption; all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: At Changping he impeached the eunuch Zhang En for unauthorized killings and the Liang-Huai salt inspector Sun Yiren for bribery; all were punished.

sentences.zh: 其秋，應龍等召還，命尚鵬兼領九邊屯務。

translations.literal: That autumn Yinglong and the others were recalled, and Shangpeng was ordered to take charge of the nine-frontier garrison-colony affairs as well.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yinglong and his colleagues were recalled, and Shangpeng was put in sole charge of garrison farming on all nine frontiers.

sentences.zh: 疏列鹽政二十事，鹺利大興。

translations.literal: In a memorial he listed twenty items on salt administration, and salt revenues greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized twenty reforms to salt policy, and salt profits rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 乃自江北躬歷九邊，先後列上屯政便宜，江北者四，薊鎮者九，遼東、宣、大者各十一，寧夏者四，甘肅者七。

translations.literal: Then, starting from Jiangbei, he personally toured the nine frontiers and submitted in succession proposals for garrison-colony policy: four for Jiangbei, nine for Jizhen, eleven each for Liaodong and Xuan-Da, four for Ningxia, and seven for Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Jiangbei to tour the nine frontiers in person, submitting practical proposals for garrison farming: four for Jiangbei, nine for Jizhen, eleven each for Liaodong and Xuan-Da, four for Ningxia, and seven for Gansu.

sentences.zh: 奏輒報可。

translations.literal: His memorials were invariably approved.
translations.idiomatic: His proposals were invariably approved.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬權既重，自負經濟才，慷慨任事。

translations.literal: Shangpeng's authority was now heavy; he prided himself on his talent for statecraft and served the public cause with bold generosity.
translations.idiomatic: With his power at its height, Shangpeng trusted in his administrative gifts and threw himself into public service with bold energy.

sentences.zh: 諸御史督鹽政者以事權見奪，欲攻去之。

translations.literal: The censors who supervised salt policy, seeing their authority usurped, sought to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Censors charged with salt supervision, feeling their authority had been stripped away, plotted to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 河東巡鹽郜永春劾尚鵬行事乖違，吏部尚書楊博議留之。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchun, the Hedong salt inspector, impeached Shangpeng for irregular conduct; Minister of Personnel Yang Bo argued that he should be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong salt inspector Gao Yongchun impeached Shangpeng for misconduct, but Minister of Personnel Yang Bo recommended keeping him in office.

sentences.zh: 會中官惡博，激帝怒，譙讓，罷博而落尚鵬職，汰屯鹽都御史官。

translations.literal: It happened that palace eunuchs hated Bo, stirred the emperor's anger, and provoked rebuke; Bo was dismissed, Shangpeng was demoted, and the office of Censor-in-Chief for garrison colonies and salt was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs who hated Bo goaded the emperor into a rage; Bo was dismissed, Shangpeng was stripped of his post, and the special censorate for garrison colonies and salt was abolished.

sentences.zh: 時三年十二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the twelfth month of the third year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the twelfth month of the third year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 明年，復坐按浙時驗進宮幣不中程，斥為民。

translations.literal: The next year he was again punished because, when investigating Zhejiang, the tribute coins he inspected for delivery to the palace failed to meet standard, and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again punished: while investigating Zhejiang he had certified palace tribute coins that failed inspection, and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，御史計坤亨等交薦，保定巡撫宋纁亦白其無罪。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Censor Ji Kunheng and others jointly recommended him, and Song Xu, governor of Baoding, also reported that he was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzong's accession, Censor Ji Kunheng and others repeatedly recommended him, and Baoding governor Song Xu also declared him innocent.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年冬，始以故官撫福建。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Wanli he was at last appointed to his former rank as grand coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 4 he was finally restored to his former rank as grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲逋餉銀，推行一條鞭法。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit overdue levy silver and to implement the single-whip method of taxation.
translations.idiomatic: He secured remission of overdue levy payments and introduced the single-whip tax reform.

sentences.zh: 劾罷總兵官胡守仁，屬吏咸奉職。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed Regional Commander Hu Shouren, and all subordinate officials thereafter performed their duties properly.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed Regional Commander Hu Shouren, after which his subordinates all performed their duties faithfully.

sentences.zh: 張居正奪情，重譴言者。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng sought to leave mourning and resume office, those who remonstrated were heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng sought to shorten his mourning and remain in power, those who protested were harshly punished.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬移書救，居正深銜之。

translations.literal: Shangpeng sent a letter in their defense; Juzheng deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng wrote in their defense, and Juzheng bore a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 會拜左副都御史，居正令吏科陳三謨以給由歲月有誤劾之，遂罷去。

translations.literal: Just as he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Juzheng had Chen Sanmo of the Personnel Section of the Censorate impeach him on the ground that the dates on his appointment credentials were wrong, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after his appointment as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Juzheng had Chen Sanmo of the Personnel Section impeach him for errors in the dates on his appointment papers, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 家居四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home four years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for four years and then died.

sentences.zh: 浙江、福建暨其鄉廣東皆以徭輕故德尚鵬，立祠祀。

translations.literal: Zhejiang, Fujian, and his native Guangdong all honored Shangpeng because corvée burdens had been lightened under him, and erected shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang, Fujian, and his native Guangdong all revered him for easing corvée burdens and erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，賜謚惠敏。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the temple name Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the epithet Huimin, meaning Benevolent and Keen.

sentences.zh: 宋儀望，字望之，吉安永豐人。

translations.literal: Song Yiwang, courtesy name Wangzhi, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yiwang, styled Wangzhi, came from Yongfeng in Ji'an prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Jiajing 26.

sentences.zh: 授吳縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 民輸白糧京師，輒破家。

translations.literal: When the people transported white grain to the capital, they were often ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Transporting tribute grain to the capital routinely ruined local households.

sentences.zh: 儀望令諸區各出公田，計役授田贍之。

translations.literal: Yiwang ordered each district to contribute public fields, calculated corvée obligations, and assigned fields to support the transport laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang had each district set aside public land, apportioned duties by labor quota, and assigned fields to support those who carried grain to the capital.

sentences.zh: 禁火葬，創子遊祠，建書院，惠績甚著。

translations.literal: He forbade cremation, founded the Ziyou Shrine, built an academy, and his benevolent achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: He banned cremation, founded the Ziyou Shrine, established an academy, and won wide renown for his benevolent administration.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 劾大將軍仇鸞挾寇自重，疏留中。

translations.literal: He impeached Grand General Qiu Luan for using the enemy to aggrandize himself; the memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Grand General Qiu Luan for exploiting the border threat to build his own power; the memorial was shelved at court.

sentences.zh: 已，陳時務十二策。

translations.literal: Later he presented twelve policies on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted twelve policy proposals on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽河東，請開桑乾河通宣、大餉道，言：「河發源金龍池下甕城驛古定橋，會眾水，東流千餘里，入盧溝橋。

translations.literal: While inspecting salt in Hedong, he requested opening the Sanggan River to serve as a supply route for Xuan-Da, saying: 'The river rises below Golden Dragon Pool at the ancient Ding Bridge by Wengcheng Post Station, gathers many streams, flows east more than a thousand li, and enters Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On salt inspection duty in Hedong he petitioned to open the Sanggan River as a supply route to Xuanfu and Datong, writing: 'The river rises below Golden Dragon Pool at the ancient Ding Bridge by Wengcheng Post, gathers tributary streams, flows east for more than a thousand li, and reaches Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其間惟大同卜村有叢石，宣府黑龍灣石崖稍險，然不逾五十里，水淺者猶二三尺，疏鑿甚易。

translations.literal: Along its course only at Bucun in Datong are there clustered rocks, and at Heilongwan in Xuanfu the stone cliffs are somewhat perilous, yet this extends no more than fifty li; where the water is shallow it is still two or three chi deep, and dredging would be very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Only at Bucun in Datong are there rock clusters, and at Heilongwan in Xuanfu the cliffs are somewhat steep—but these obstacles span no more than fifty li, and even the shallowest stretches are still two or three feet deep, so dredging would be straightforward.

sentences.zh: 曩大同巡撫侯鉞嘗乘小艇赴懷來，歷卜村、黑龍灣，安行無虞。

translations.literal: Formerly Grand Coordinator Hou Yue of Datong once took a small boat to Huailai, passing through Bucun and Heilongwan without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Former Datong grand coordinator Hou Yue had once taken a small boat to Huailai, passing Bucun and Heilongwan without mishap.

sentences.zh: 又自懷來溯流，載米三十石達之古定河，足利漕可徵。」

translations.literal: Again, from Huailai he went upstream and carried thirty shi of grain to Guding River, sufficient proof that grain transport could be made profitable.'
translations.idiomatic: From Huailai he had also gone upstream and delivered thirty shi of grain to Guding River—enough to show that profitable grain transport was feasible.'

sentences.zh: 時方行挖運，率三十石致一石。

translations.literal: At that time overland transport was in use, and on average thirty shi were expended to deliver one shi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time overland haulage was standard, and it typically took thirty shi of effort to deliver one shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 儀望疏至，下廷議。

translations.literal: When Yiwang's memorial arrived, it was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiwang's memorial reached court, it was referred for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書聶豹言：「河成便漕，兼制敵騎。」

translations.literal: Minister of War Nie Bao said: 'If the river is opened, grain transport will be convenient and enemy cavalry can also be checked.」
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Nie Bao argued: 'Opening the river would ease grain transport and also help contain enemy cavalry.」

sentences.zh: 工部尚書歐陽必進言：「道遠役重。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Ouyang Bijin said: 「The route is long and the labor burden heavy.」'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Ouyang Bijin countered: 「The route is too long and the labor burden too heavy.」'

sentences.zh: 遂報罷。

translations.literal: The proposal was then reported rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was rejected.

sentences.zh: 儀望尋省母歸。

translations.literal: Yiwang soon went home to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang soon left office to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 還朝，發胡宗憲、阮鶚奸貪狀，鶚被逮。

translations.literal: On returning to court he exposed the corruption of Hu Zongxian and Ruan E; E was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he exposed the corruption of Hu Zongxian and Ruan E; Ruan was arrested.

sentences.zh: 二人皆嚴嵩私人，嵩由是不悅。

translations.literal: Both men were private associates of Yan Song, and Song was displeased on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Both were protégés of Yan Song, who took offense at the attack.

sentences.zh: 及受命督三殿門工，嵩子世蕃私賈人金，屬必進俾與工事，儀望執不可。

translations.literal: When he was ordered to supervise work on the gates of the Three Halls, Song's son Shifan privately took a merchant's gold and asked Bijin to let him join the project; Yiwang firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When he was assigned to supervise construction on the Three Halls gates, Shifan—Yan Song's son—took a bribe from a merchant and asked Bijin to let him into the contract; Yiwang refused.

sentences.zh: 工竣，敘勞，擢大理右寺丞。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was completed, his service was rewarded with promotion to Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 世蕃以為德，儀望請急歸，無所謝，世蕃益怒。

translations.literal: Shifan regarded this as a favor owed, but Yiwang requested urgent leave to return home and offered no thanks; Shifan grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan took this as a debt owed him, but Yiwang asked for urgent leave to go home and offered no thanks—so Shifan grew even angrier.

sentences.zh: 會災異考察京官，必進遷吏部，遂坐以浮躁，貶夷陵判官。

translations.literal: When omens prompted an evaluation of capital officials, Bijin was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and Yiwang was punished for frivolity and demoted to assistant magistrate of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: During a review of capital officials prompted by omens, Bijin was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and Yiwang was found guilty of rashness and demoted to assistant magistrate of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，擢霸州兵備僉事。

translations.literal: When Song fell, Yiwang was promoted to Military Intendant of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Song's fall he was promoted to Military Intendant of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 請城涿州，除馬戶逋稅。

translations.literal: He requested fortifying Zhuozhou and remitting overdue taxes owed by horse-rearing households.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to fortify Zhuozhou and cancel overdue taxes on horse-breeding households.

sentences.zh: 進大名兵備副使，改福建。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Daming and then transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Military Affairs at Daming, then transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 與總兵官戚繼光合兵破倭，因列海防善後事。

translations.literal: Together with Regional Commander Qi Jiguang he combined forces and defeated the Japanese pirates, then listed measures for consolidating coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Regional Commander Qi Jiguang to defeat the pirates and then submitted a program for consolidating coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 詔從其請。

translations.literal: An edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposals.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，吏部尚書楊博欲黜儀望，考功郎劉一儒持之，乃鐫二秩，補四川僉事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo wished to dismiss Yiwang; Review Section Director Liu Yiru held firm for him, and he was instead reduced two ranks and appointed Commissioner in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 2, Minister Yang Bo sought to dismiss Yiwang, but Review Director Liu Yiru intervened; Yiwang was reduced two ranks instead and appointed a commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，張居正當國，雅知儀望才，擢右僉都御史，巡撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng held power and had long known Yiwang's talent; he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of the prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2, with Zhang Juzheng in power, Yiwang—whose ability Juzheng had long respected—was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of the Yingtian region.

sentences.zh: 奏減屬郡災賦。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce disaster levies in subordinate prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He secured reductions in disaster levies across his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 海警稍定，將吏諱言兵，儀望與副使王叔果修戰備。

translations.literal: Coastal alarms had somewhat subsided, and officers were reluctant to speak of military matters; Yiwang and Vice Commissioner Wang Shuguo nevertheless repaired war preparations.
translations.idiomatic: With coastal threats easing, officers avoided discussing military readiness; Yiwang and Vice Commissioner Wang Shuguo nonetheless rebuilt defenses.

sentences.zh: 倭果至，禦之黑水洋，斬獲多，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Japanese raiders did arrive; he met them at Heishuiyang, killed and captured many, and was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates did appear; he met them at Heishuiyang, inflicted heavy casualties, and was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先有詔雪建文諸臣，儀望創表忠祠祀之南京。

translations.literal: An edict had earlier rehabilitated the officials of the Jianwen reign; Yiwang founded the Shrine of Loyalty in Nanjing to worship them.
translations.idiomatic: After an edict rehabilitated the officials who had served Emperor Jianwen, Yiwang founded the Shrine of Loyal Remembrance in Nanjing to honor them.

sentences.zh: 宋忠臣楊邦晙，儀望鄉人也，葬江寧，歲久漸湮，儀望為封其墓，載其祠祀典。

translations.literal: Yang Bangjun, a loyal minister of Song and a fellow townsman of Yiwang, was buried in Jiangning; after many years the grave was gradually lost. Yiwang had the tomb restored and entered his shrine in the register of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bangjun, a Song loyalist and fellow townsman, lay buried in Jiangning until his grave faded from memory; Yiwang restored the tomb and secured his place in the official sacrificial register.

sentences.zh: 故太常卿袁洪愈、祭酒姜寶皆不為居正所喜，儀望薦之朝，漸失居正意。

translations.literal: The former Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Hongyu and Libationer Jiang Bao were both disliked by Juzheng; Yiwang recommended them to court and gradually lost Juzheng's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Former Director of Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Hongyu and Libationer Jiang Bao were both out of favor with Juzheng; when Yiwang recommended them to court he gradually lost Juzheng's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 四年，稍遷南京大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was gradually transferred to be Director of the Court of Judicial Review at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to serve as Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逾年改北，被劾罷歸。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the north, was impeached, dismissed, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was moved to the northern capital, impeached, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 儀望少師聶豹，私淑王守仁，又從鄒守益、歐陽德、羅洪先遊。

translations.literal: Yiwang in youth studied under Nie Bao, privately revered Wang Shouren, and also associated with Zou Shouyi, Ouyang De, and Luo Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yiwang studied under Nie Bao, privately revered Wang Yangming, and also learned from Zou Shouyi, Ouyang De, and Luo Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 守仁從祀，儀望有力焉。

translations.literal: When Shouren was admitted to the temple of worthies, Yiwang had been influential in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang had played a significant role in securing Wang Yangming's admission to the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 家居數年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home several years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for several years and then died.

sentences.zh: 張嶽，字汝宗，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, courtesy name Ruzong, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, styled Ruzong, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Jiajing 38.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed a courier-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier-attendant in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 巡視內府庫藏，奏行厘弊八事。

translations.literal: While inspecting the inner palace treasuries, he memorialized and implemented eight measures to rectify abuses.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the inner palace treasuries he proposed eight reforms to curb abuses, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 已，又陳時政，極言講學者以富貴功名鼓動士大夫，談虛論寂，靡然成風。

translations.literal: Later he again addressed current policy, vehemently stating that lecturers in moral philosophy stirred officials with prospects of wealth, rank, and fame, and that empty talk of quietism had become the prevailing fashion.
translations.idiomatic: He later addressed current affairs again, sharply criticizing moral philosophers who stirred officials with promises of wealth and office and had made empty talk of quietism the fashion of the day.

sentences.zh: 又今吏治方清，獨兵部無振刷，推用總兵黃印、韓承慶等，非庸即狡。

translations.literal: Moreover, civil administration was now being rectified, yet the Ministry of War alone showed no renewal; those it promoted as regional commanders, such as Huang Yin and Han Chengqing, were either mediocre or cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Civil administration was being cleaned up, he added, but the Ministry of War showed no similar renewal: regional commanders it promoted, such as Huang Yin and Han Chengqing, were either mediocre or cunning.

sentences.zh: 曹司條例淆亂無章，胥吏朋奸，搏噬將校，其咎必有所歸。

translations.literal: Department regulations were confused and without order; clerks formed factions of corruption and preyed on officers; responsibility for this must lie somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Department regulations were in disorder, clerks formed corrupt factions that preyed on officers, and someone had to be held accountable.

sentences.zh: 時徐階當國，為講學會，而楊博在兵部，意蓋指二人也。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jie held power and was head of a lecture society, while Yang Bo was at the Ministry of War; the intent was plainly directed at the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jie held power and led a lecture society, while Yang Bo headed the Ministry of War—the criticism was plainly aimed at both men.

sentences.zh: 博奏辨乞罷，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized in defense and asked to resign; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Bo defended himself in a memorial asking to resign; the emperor reassured him and kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 博自是惡嶽。

translations.literal: From then on Bo hated Yue.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Bo bore a grudge against Yue.

sentences.zh: 及掌吏部，嶽已遷工科左給事中，遂出為雲南參議。

translations.literal: When he took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Yue had already been transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Works Section, and was then sent out as Administrative Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Yue had already moved to Left Supervising Secretary in the Works Section and was then posted out as Administrative Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南參政。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正雅知嶽，用為太僕少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng, who had long known Yue's ability, appointed him Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign Zhang Juzheng, who had long respected Yue, appointed him Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京右僉都御史，督操江。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and supervised the Caojiang naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing with charge of the Yangtze naval command.

sentences.zh: 甫到官，會居正父喪謀奪情，南京尚書潘晟及諸給事、御史，咸上疏請留居正。

translations.literal: He had just taken office when Juzheng, upon his father's death, sought to shorten mourning and remain in power; Minister Pan Sheng at Nanjing and the supervising secretaries and censors all memorialized asking that Juzheng be retained.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken office when Juzheng sought to shorten mourning after his father's death; Nanjing Minister Pan Sheng and the supervising secretaries and censors all petitioned to keep him in power.

sentences.zh: 嶽獨馳疏請令馳驛奔喪，居正大怒。

translations.literal: Yue alone sent an urgent memorial asking that Juzheng be ordered to rush home by relay post for the funeral; Juzheng was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Yue alone sent an urgent memorial demanding that Juzheng rush home by relay post for the funeral; Juzheng was furious.

sentences.zh: 會大計京官，給事中傅作舟等承風劾嶽，貶一秩調外，嶽遂歸。

translations.literal: When the great evaluation of capital officials came, Supervising Secretary Fu Zuozhou and others, following the prevailing wind, impeached Yue; he was demoted one rank and transferred outside the capital, and Yue then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the capital officials' evaluation, Supervising Secretary Fu Zuozhou and others took their cue from Juzheng and impeached Yue; he was demoted one rank, posted outside the capital, and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，操江僉都御史呂藿、給事中吳綰知居正憾未釋，摭劾嶽落職閑住。

translations.literal: After a long time, Caojiang Censor-in-Chief Lü Huo and Supervising Secretary Wu Wan, knowing that Juzheng's resentment had not yet subsided, gathered charges and impeached Yue, who was dismissed and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, knowing Juzheng's resentment had not faded, Caojiang Censor Lü Huo and Supervising Secretary Wu Wan dredged up charges and had Yue dismissed to idle retirement.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，居正死，南京御史方萬山薦嶽，劾作舟。

translations.literal: Only two months later Juzheng died; Nanjing Censor Fang Wanshan recommended Yue and impeached Zuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later Juzheng died; Nanjing Censor Fang Wanshan recommended Yue and impeached Fu Zuozhou.

sentences.zh: 作舟坐斥，起嶽四川參議。

translations.literal: Zuozhou was punished and dismissed; Yue was recalled as Administrative Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuozhou was dismissed, and Yue was recalled as Administrative Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Nan and Gan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入為左僉都御史，獻時政四議。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Censor-in-Chief and presented four proposals on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Left Censor-in-Chief and submitted four policy proposals.

sentences.zh: 其一言宗藩宜以世次遞殺，親盡則停，俾習四民之業。

translations.literal: One stated that imperial clansmen should be reduced in rank by generation in succession, and when kinship was exhausted the reduction should stop, so that they might learn the occupations of the four classes of people.
translations.idiomatic: One proposed that imperial clansmen should be demoted rank by rank each generation until the degree of kinship was exhausted, then allowed to take up ordinary trades.

sentences.zh: 其一言治河之策，夏鎮固當開，沽頭亦不可廢。

translations.literal: Another spoke on river-control policy: Xiazhen should indeed be opened, but Gutou also must not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Another addressed river control: opening Xiazhen was necessary, but abandoning Gutou was not.

sentences.zh: 並報寢。

translations.literal: All were reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: All were shelved without action.

sentences.zh: 進左副都御史，上疏評議廷臣賢否，為給事中袁國臣等所論。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and submitted a memorial appraising which court officials were worthy and which were not; he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Yuan Guochen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he submitted a memorial ranking court officials as worthy or unworthy and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Yuan Guochen and others.

sentences.zh: 時已遷刑部右侍郎，坐罷歸。

translations.literal: By then he had already been transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice; on this charge he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been made Right Vice Minister of Justice; on these charges he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 李材，字孟誠，豐城人，尚書遂子也。

translations.literal: Li Cai, styled Mengcheng, was a man of Fengcheng and the son of the Minister Su Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cai, courtesy name Mengcheng, was a native of Fengcheng and the son of Minister Su Sui.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖四十一年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of the Jiajing reign and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of Jiajing and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 素從鄒守益講學。

translations.literal: He had long followed Zou Shouyi in the study of learning.
translations.idiomatic: He had long studied under Zou Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 自以學未成，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Considering that his learning was not yet complete, he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling his studies were still unfinished, he asked for leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 訪唐樞、王畿、錢德洪，與問難。

translations.literal: He visited Tang Shu, Wang Ji, and Qian Dehong, engaging them in questioning and debate.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Tang Shu, Wang Ji, and Qian Dehong, debating and testing his understanding with them.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中還朝。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 由兵部郎中稍遷廣東僉事。

translations.literal: From a director in the Ministry of War he was gradually promoted to assistant commissioner in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a director in the Ministry of War, he was gradually promoted to assistant commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 羅旁賊猖獗，材襲破之周高山，設屯以守。

translations.literal: The Luopang bandits were rampant; Cai made a surprise attack and broke them at Mount Zhougao, establishing garrison colonies to hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: The Luopang bandits were running wild; Cai struck and routed them at Mount Zhougao, then established garrison farms to hold the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊有三巢在新會境，調副總兵梁守愚由恩平，遊擊王瑞由德慶入，身出肇慶中道，夜半斬賊五百級，毀廬舍千餘，空其地，募人田之。

translations.literal: The bandits had three lairs within the borders of Xinhui. He dispatched the vice commander-in-chief Liang Shouyu by way of Enping and the mobile corps commander Wang Rui by way of Deqing, while he himself set out from Zhaoqing along the middle route. At midnight they beheaded five hundred bandits, destroyed more than a thousand dwellings, emptied the land, and recruited people to farm it.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits maintained three strongholds in Xinhui territory. Cai sent Vice Commander-in-Chief Liang Shouyu in from Enping and Mobile Corps Commander Wang Rui from Deqing, while he himself marched out of Zhaoqing along the central route. At midnight they took five hundred heads, burned more than a thousand buildings, cleared the land, and brought in settlers to cultivate it.

sentences.zh: 亡何，倭五千攻陷電白，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Before long, five thousand Japanese pirates attacked and captured Dianbai, plundered on a great scale, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, five thousand Japanese raiders stormed Dianbai, looted the place thoroughly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 材追破之石城，設伏海口，伺其遁而殲之，奪還婦女三千餘。

translations.literal: Cai pursued and defeated them at Shicheng, set an ambush at Haikou, waited for their retreat and annihilated them, and recovered more than three thousand women.
translations.idiomatic: Cai pursued them, broke them at Shicheng, laid an ambush at Haikou, and wiped them out as they fled, recovering more than three thousand captive women.

sentences.zh: 會奸人引倭自黃山間道潰而東。

translations.literal: Just then, wicked men guided the Japanese through a bypath at Huangshan, and they broke out eastward.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment, traitors led the Japanese through a hidden pass at Huangshan, and they burst through toward the east.

sentences.zh: 材聲言大軍數道至以疑賊，而返故道迎擊，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Cai loudly proclaimed that large armies were arriving by several routes to confuse the bandits, then returned by the original road to meet and strike them, killing them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cai spread word that large imperial forces were closing in from several directions to unsettle the enemy, then doubled back along the old route to intercept them and killed every man.

sentences.zh: 又追襲雷州倭至英利，皆遁去，降賊渠許恩於陽江。

translations.literal: He again pursued and struck the Japanese pirates of Leizhou as far as Yingli; they all fled. At Yangjiang he accepted the surrender of the bandit chieftain Xu En.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the Leizhou pirates all the way to Yingli; they all fled. At Yangjiang he accepted the surrender of the bandit leader Xu En.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進副使。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered on the rolls, and he was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正柄國，不悅材，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wanli reign, Zhang Juzheng held power in the state and was displeased with Cai, whereupon Cai pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli, Zhang Juzheng dominated the government and took a dislike to Cai, who then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，起官山東。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Cai was recalled to office in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, Cai was recalled to serve in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以才調遼東開原。

translations.literal: Because of his talent he was transferred to Kaiyuan in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his ability he was transferred to Kaiyuan in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雲南洱海參政，進按察使，備兵金騰。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was moved to serve as administrative commissioner of Erhai in Yunnan, promoted to surveillance commissioner, and charged with military defense at Jinteng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrative commissioner at Erhai in Yunnan, then promoted to surveillance commissioner with military responsibility over Jinteng.

sentences.zh: 金騰地接緬甸，而孟養、蠻莫兩土司介其間，叛服不常。

translations.literal: Jinteng bordered Burma, while the two native offices of Mengyang and Manmo lay between them, their submission and rebellion never constant.
translations.idiomatic: Jinteng bordered Burma, with the native offices of Mengyang and Manmo lying between them—forever shifting between loyalty and revolt.

sentences.zh: 緬部目曰大曩長、曰散奪者，率數千人據其地。

translations.literal: Among the Burmese subordinate chiefs were one called Dalangchang and one called Saneduo, who led several thousand men in occupying that territory.
translations.idiomatic: Two Burmese subordinate chiefs, Dalangchang and Saneduo, led several thousand men in seizing the region.

sentences.zh: 材謂不收兩土司無以制緬，遣人招兩土司來歸，而間討抗命夷阿坡。

translations.literal: Cai said that unless the two native offices were recovered there would be no means of controlling Burma; he sent men to summon the two native offices to return to allegiance, while at the same time moving to punish the rebellious tribesman Apo.
translations.idiomatic: Cai argued that without winning back the two native offices he could not check Burma. He sent envoys to bring them back into allegiance while simultaneously moving against the defiant tribesman Apo.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，緬遣兵爭蠻莫，材合兩土司兵敗緬眾，殺大曩長，逐散奪去。

translations.literal: Before long, Burma sent troops to contest Manmo; Cai combined the forces of the two native offices, defeated the Burmese host, killed Dalangchang, and drove Saneduo away.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Burma sent troops to seize Manmo. Cai joined forces with the two native offices, routed the Burmese army, killed Dalangchang, and drove off Saneduo.

sentences.zh: 緬帥莽應裏益兵至孟養，復擊沈其舟，斬其將一人，乃退。

translations.literal: The Burmese commander Mang Yingli reinforced his army at Mengyang; Cai again attacked, sank their boats, beheaded one of their generals, and then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese commander Mang Yingli reinforced at Mengyang. Cai struck again, sank their boats, killed one of their generals, and forced them to retreat.

sentences.zh: 有猛密者，地在緬境，數為緬侵奪，舉族內徙，有司居之戶碗。

translations.literal: There was a place called Mengmi, whose territory lay within the Burmese border and had repeatedly been seized by Burma; the whole clan moved inward, and the local authorities resettled them at Huwan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengmi lay within Burmese territory and had been repeatedly overrun by Burma. Its people had moved en masse into Ming lands, and the authorities resettled them at Huwan.

sentences.zh: 至是，緬勢稍屈，材資遣還故土。

translations.literal: By this time Burmese power had slackened somewhat, and Cai supplied resources and sent them back to their original lands.
translations.idiomatic: By then Burmese strength had waned somewhat, and Cai furnished supplies to send the people back to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 亡何，緬人驅象陣大舉復仇，兩土司告急。

translations.literal: Before long the Burmese drove elephant formations and launched a great campaign of revenge; the two native offices sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the Burmese marched in force with elephant columns to take revenge, and the two native offices cried for help.

sentences.zh: 材遣遊擊劉天俸率把總寇崇德等出威緬，渡金沙江，與孟養兵會遮浪，迎擊之。

translations.literal: Cai dispatched the mobile corps commander Liu Tianfu, leading the garrison commanders Kou Chongde and others out through Weimian, crossed the Jinsha River, joined the Mengyang troops at Zhelang, and met the enemy in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cai sent Mobile Corps Commander Liu Tianfu with garrison commanders including Kou Chongde through Weimian, across the Jinsha River, to join Mengyang forces at Zhelang and meet the enemy head-on.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，生擒繡衣賊將三人。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly defeated, and three enemy generals in embroidered robes were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was routed, and three enemy generals in embroidered robes were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉世曾、總兵官沐昌祚以大捷聞，詔令覆勘。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Liu Shizeng and the regional commander Mu Changzuo reported the great victory; an edict ordered a re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Shizeng and Regional Commander Mu Changzuo reported a great victory, and the throne ordered the claims verified.

sentences.zh: 未上，而材擢右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: Before the report had been submitted, Cai was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed to govern and pacify Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before the report even went up, Cai was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed to govern Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 材好講學，遣部卒供生徒役，卒多怨。

translations.literal: Cai loved to gather disciples and lecture on learning; he had his troops serve the students, and the soldiers greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai loved to lecture and kept a circle of students, assigning his troops to wait on them—a duty the soldiers deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 又徇諸生請，改參將公署為學宮。

translations.literal: He also yielded to the students' request and converted the brigade commander's official residence into a school.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave in to the students' petition and turned the brigade commander's headquarters into a school.

sentences.zh: 參將米萬春諷門卒梅林等大噪，馳入城，縱囚毀諸生廬，直趨軍門，挾賞銀四千，洶洶不解。

translations.literal: The brigade commander Mi Wanchun incited the gate guards Meilin and others to raise a great uproar; they galloped into the city, released prisoners, destroyed the students' quarters, marched straight to headquarters, seized four thousand taels of reward silver, and in a tumult refused to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Mi Wanchun goaded gate guards led by Meilin into open mutiny. They galloped into the city, freed prisoners, wrecked the students' lodgings, marched on headquarters, and demanded four thousand taels in reward silver, roaring and refusing to stand down.

sentences.zh: 居二日，萬春脅材更軍中不便十二事，令上疏歸罪副使丁惟寧、知府沈鈇等，材隱忍從之。

translations.literal: After two days, Wanchun coerced Cai into altering twelve inconvenient military regulations and ordered him to memorialize placing blame on the vice commissioner Ding Weining, the prefect Shen Fu, and others; Cai endured it in silence and complied.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Wanchun forced Cai to rewrite twelve military regulations to the army's liking and submit a memorial blaming Vice Commissioner Ding Weining, Prefect Shen Fu, and others. Cai swallowed the humiliation and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 惟寧責數萬春，萬春欲殺惟寧，跳而免，材遂復劾惟寧激變。

translations.literal: Weining rebuked Wanchun at length; Wanchun wanted to kill Weining, who leaped away and escaped, whereupon Cai again impeached Weining for provoking the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Weining sharply rebuked Wanchun, who tried to kill him; Weining leapt aside and escaped. Cai then impeached Weining again, accusing him of provoking the uprising.

sentences.zh: 詔下鈇等吏，貶惟寧三官，材還籍候勘。

translations.literal: An edict subjected Shen Fu and the others to judicial inquiry, demoted Weining three ranks, and ordered Cai to return to his native place pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Shen Fu and the others before the courts, demoted Weining three ranks, and sent Cai home to await investigation.

sentences.zh: 時十五年十一月也。

translations.literal: This was in the eleventh month of the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was the eleventh month of the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 御史楊紹程勘萬春首亂，宜罪。

translations.literal: The censor Yang Shaocheng investigated and found that Wanchun had been the first to incite the rebellion and ought to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Shaocheng investigated and concluded that Wanchun had instigated the rebellion and deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行庇之，置不問，旋調天津善地去。

translations.literal: The grand secretary Shen Shixing shielded him, set the matter aside without inquiry, and soon had him transferred to a comfortable post in Tianjin and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing protected him, dropped the case, and soon transferred him to a soft posting in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 而材又以雲南事被訐，遂獲重譴。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Cai was again denounced over the Yunnan affair and thus received severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, meanwhile, was denounced over the Yunnan campaign and received harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔勘征緬功，巡按御史蘇贊阝言斬馘不及千，破城拓地皆無驗，猛密地尚為緬據，材、天俸等虛張功伐，副使陳嚴之與相附和，宜並罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had ordered an investigation of the merits of the Burma campaign. The touring censor Su Zan reported that the count of beheaded enemy did not reach a thousand, that claims of capturing cities and expanding territory were all unverified, that the land of Mengmi was still held by Burma, and that Cai, Tianfu, and others had inflated their achievements while the vice commissioner Chen Yan'zhi had colluded with them—all of whom ought to be punished together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered the Burma campaign merits investigated. Touring Censor Su Zan reported that fewer than a thousand enemy heads had been taken, that no claims of captured cities or expanded territory checked out, that Mengmi remained in Burmese hands, and that Cai, Tianfu, and others had exaggerated their victories while Vice Commissioner Chen Yan'zhi had backed them—all deserved joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，削世曾籍，奪昌祚祿一年，材、嚴之、天俸俱逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; he stripped Liu Shizeng of his registration, docked Mu Changzuo's salary for one year, and had Cai, Yan'zhi, and Tianfu all arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. He struck Liu Shizeng from the rolls, cut Mu Changzuo's salary for a year, and had Cai, Yan'zhi, and Tianfu arrested and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書李世達、左都御史吳時來、大理少卿李棟等，當材、天俸徒，嚴之鐫秩。

translations.literal: The minister of punishments Li Shida, the left censor-in-chief Wu Shilai, the vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review Li Dong, and others recommended exile for Cai and Tianfu and reduction of rank for Yan'zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Li Shida, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai, Court of Judicial Review Vice Minister Li Dong, and others recommended exile for Cai and Tianfu and a reduction of rank for Yan'zhi.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，奪郎中、御史、寺正諸臣俸，典詔獄李登雲等亦解官。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he suspended the salaries of the directors, censors, and tribunal officials, and Li Dengyun, superintendent of the imperial prison, and others were also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased. He suspended the salaries of the recommending directors, censors, and tribunal officials, and dismissed Li Dengyun, superintendent of the imperial prison, and others.

sentences.zh: 於是改擬遣戍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sentence was revised to exile to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict was then revised to exile on frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 特旨引紅牌說謊例，坐材、天俸斬，嚴之除名。

translations.literal: By special edict, citing the precedent of the red-placard lying case, Cai and Tianfu were sentenced to decapitation, and Yan'zhi was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict, invoking the precedent of the red-placard perjury case, Cai and Tianfu were sentenced to decapitation and Yan'zhi was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 大學士時行等數為解，給事中唐堯欽等亦言：「材以夷攻夷，功不可泯。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries including Shixing repeatedly interceded on their behalf, and the supervising secretary Tang Yaoqin also said: 「Cai used barbarians to attack barbarians; his merit cannot be erased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shixing and others repeatedly pleaded for mercy, and Supervising Secretary Tang Yaoqin also argued: 「Cai used barbarians against barbarians—his service cannot be wiped away.

sentences.zh: 奏報偶虛，坐以死，假令盡虛無實，掩罪為功，何以罪之？

translations.literal: If a report is occasionally inflated, he is sentenced to death; suppose the report were wholly false with no substance, concealing crimes as merit—how then would one punish him?
translations.idiomatic: A little exaggeration in a report earns the death penalty? If the report were wholly false, with crimes dressed up as merit—how would you punish that?

sentences.zh: 設不幸失城池，全軍不返，又何以罪之？」

translations.literal: If, unhappily, he lost cities and fortresses and the whole army failed to return, how then would one punish him?」
translations.idiomatic: And if he had lost cities and fortresses and the entire army never came home—how would you punish that?」

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not heed any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 幽系五年，論救者五十餘疏。

translations.literal: Imprisoned in confinement for five years, more than fifty memorials pleaded for his release.
translations.idiomatic: He languished in prison for five years while more than fifty memorials pleaded for his release.

sentences.zh: 已，天俸以善用火器，釋令立功，時行等復為材申理，皆不省。

translations.literal: Later Tianfu was released because of his skill in using firearms and ordered to earn merit through service; Shixing and others again pleaded Cai's case, but all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tianfu was released on account of his mastery of firearms and told to redeem himself in battle. Shixing and others again argued Cai's case—all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 亡何，孟養使入貢，具言緬人侵軼，天朝救援，破敵有狀，聞典兵者在獄，眾皆流涕。

translations.literal: Before long a Mengyang tribute envoy arrived, fully reporting Burmese raids and the celestial court's rescue, with clear evidence of defeating the enemy; hearing that the officer who had commanded the troops was in prison, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a Mengyang tribute envoy arrived and gave a full account of Burmese incursions and the court's rescue, with proof of victories on the ground. When he said the commander sat in prison, everyone wept.

sentences.zh: 而楚雄士民閻世祥等亦相率詣闕訟冤。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the gentry and common people of Chuxiong, including Yan Shixiang, also went in groups to the palace gates to petition against the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile gentry and commoners of Chuxiong, led by Yan Shixiang, marched in groups to the palace gates to protest the injustice.

sentences.zh: 帝意乃稍解，命再勘。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger then eased somewhat, and he ordered another investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind softened somewhat, and he ordered the case reinvestigated.

sentences.zh: 勘至，材罪不掩功。

translations.literal: When the investigation was completed, Cai's faults did not outweigh his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the reinvestigation concluded, Cai's faults did not outweigh his achievements.

sentences.zh: 大學士王錫爵等再疏為言，帝故遲之，至二十一年四月，始命戍鎮海衛。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries including Wang Xinjue again memorialized on his behalf; the emperor deliberately delayed, until the fourth month of the twenty-first year, when he finally ordered exile to Zhenhai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Xinjue and others memorialized again on his behalf, but the emperor deliberately dragged his feet. Not until the fourth month of the twenty-first year did he finally order Cai exiled to Zhenhai Guard.

sentences.zh: 材所至，輒聚徒講學，學者稱見羅先生。

translations.literal: Wherever Cai went he would gather disciples and lecture on learning; scholars called him Master Jianluo.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Cai went he gathered students and taught; scholars called him Master Jianluo.

sentences.zh: 系獄時，就問者不絕。

translations.literal: While imprisoned, those who came to seek instruction never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Even in prison, students came to him without end.

sentences.zh: 至戍所，學徒益眾。

translations.literal: When he reached his place of exile, his disciples grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile his following only grew.

sentences.zh: 許孚遠方巡撫福建，日相過從，材以此忘羈旅。

translations.literal: Xu Fuyuan was then touring as grand coordinator of Fujian; they visited each other daily, and through this Cai forgot the hardship of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fuyuan was then touring as grand coordinator of Fujian; they saw each other daily, and in his company Cai forgot the ache of banishment.

sentences.zh: 久之赦還。

translations.literal: After a long time he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was pardoned and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 陸樹德，字與成，尚書樹聲弟也。

translations.literal: Lu Shude, styled Yucheng, was the younger brother of the minister Lu Shusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shude, courtesy name Yucheng, was the younger brother of Minister Lu Shusheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree at the end of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除嚴州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 行取當授給事、御史，會樹聲拜侍郎，乃授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Selected for central appointment, he should have been made a supervising secretary or censor, but as Shusheng had just been appointed vice minister, he was instead made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for promotion to the capital, he would normally have received a post as supervising secretary or censor, but because Shusheng had just become a vice minister he was instead made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，改禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Longqing he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 穆宗御朝講，不發一語。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong attended court lectures but did not utter a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong attended court lectures but never spoke a word.

sentences.zh: 樹德言：「上下交為泰，今暌隔若此，何以劘君德，訓萬幾？」

translations.literal: Shude said: 「When ruler and subject exchange freely there is flourishing; with estrangement such as this now, how can the ruler's virtue be sharpened and the myriad affairs of state be instructed?」
translations.idiomatic: Shude said: 「When ruler and minister speak freely together, the realm flourishes. With this wall between you, how can Your Majesty hone his virtue or guide the myriad affairs of state?」

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He received no answer.

sentences.zh: 屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly until he became supervising secretary-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，詔輟東宮講讀，樹德言：「自四月迄八月，為時甚遙，請非盛暑，仍御講筵。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, an edict suspended the crown prince's lectures; Shude said: 「From the fourth month until the eighth, the interval is very long; I ask that outside the height of summer Your Majesty still attend the lecture hall.」
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year an edict suspended the crown prince's lectures. Shude said: 「From the fourth month to the eighth is a long gap; I beg that, except in the worst heat of summer, Your Majesty continue the lecture hall.」

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 穆宗頗倦勤，樹德言：「日月交蝕，旱魃為災，當及時修省。」

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong grew somewhat weary of governing; Shude said: 「Solar and lunar eclipses have occurred, and the drought demon has brought calamity; one ought timely to examine oneself and reform.」
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong grew weary of governing. Shude said: 「The sun and moon have been eclipsed, and drought demons have brought disaster—the court should repent and reform at once.」

sentences.zh: 及帝不豫，又請謹藥餌，善保護，仲夏亢陽月，宜益慎起居。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, he again asked that medicines be taken with care and that he be well protected; in the midsummer month of blazing heat, one ought all the more to be careful in daily regimen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, he urged careful use of medicine and proper care of the imperial person: in the blazing midsummer heat, daily regimen deserved still greater caution.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，疏皆留中。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, and the memorials were all withheld in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, and every memorial was shelved without reply.

sentences.zh: 內臣請祈福戒壇，已得旨，樹德言：「戒壇度僧，男女擾雜，導淫傷化。

translations.literal: Inner court eunuchs requested a Buddhist fasting altar for prayers; the edict had already been granted when Shude said: 「At fasting altars monks are ordained, men and women mingle in disorder, leading to debauchery and harm to public morals.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs asked to set up a Buddhist fasting altar for blessings; the request had already been approved when Shude said: 「Fasting altars ordain monks, men and women crowd together in confusion, and debauchery undermines public morals.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲保聖躬，宜法大禹之惡旨酒，成湯之不邇聲色，何必奉佛。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to preserve the sacred person, one ought to follow Yu the Great in abhorring strong wine and King Tang in keeping far from music and women—why must one serve the Buddha?」
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to preserve his health, follow Yu the Great's hatred of strong wine and King Tang's distance from music and women—why turn to Buddhism?」

sentences.zh: 未幾，穆宗崩，神宗嗣位，中官馮保擠司禮孟沖而代之。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Muzong died; Emperor Shenzong succeeded to the throne, and the eunuch Feng Bao displaced Meng Chong of the Directorate of Ceremonial and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Muzong died and Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne. The eunuch Feng Bao pushed aside Meng Chong of the Directorate of Ceremonial and took his place.

sentences.zh: 樹德言：「先帝甫崩，忽傳馮保掌司禮監。

translations.literal: Shude said: 「The late emperor had just died when it was suddenly announced that Feng Bao would head the Directorate of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Shude said: 「The late emperor had barely died when word suddenly came that Feng Bao would head the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 果先帝意，何不傳示數日前，乃在彌留後？

translations.literal: If this truly was the late emperor's wish, why was it not proclaimed several days earlier, and only after his final illness?
translations.idiomatic: If this truly reflected the late emperor's wish, why proclaim it only after his death throes, and not days before?

sentences.zh: 果陛下意，則哀痛方深，萬幾未御，何暇念中官？」

translations.literal: If it is Your Majesty's wish, then grief is still deep and the myriad affairs of state are not yet handled—what leisure is there to think of eunuchs?」
translations.idiomatic: If it is Your Majesty's own wish, then grief is still fresh and state affairs lie untouched—what moment is this to worry over eunuchs?」

sentences.zh: 疏入，保大恨。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Bao greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Feng Bao hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 比議祧廟，樹德請毋祧宣宗，仍祀睿宗世室，格不行。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple succession was under discussion, Shude asked that Xuanzong not be elevated in the temple line and that Ruizong's spirit shrine continue to be worshipped; the proposal was rejected and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated ancestral temple succession, Shude argued against elevating Xuanzong in the line and for keeping Ruizong's spirit shrine—his proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 已，極陳民運白糧之患，請領之漕臣，從之。

translations.literal: Later he thoroughly set forth the evils of civilian transport of white-grain tribute and asked that it be placed under the canal transport officials; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out at length the abuses of civilian transport of white-grain tribute and asked that canal transport officials take charge—the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 樹德居言職三年，疏數十上，率侃直。

translations.literal: Shude held the office of remonstrance for three years, submitting several dozen memorials, mostly bold and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Shude spent three years in the remonstrance offices, submitting dozens of memorials, almost all of them blunt and direct.

sentences.zh: 會樹聲掌禮部，乃量遷尚寶卿。

translations.literal: When Shusheng took charge of the Ministry of Rites, Shude was modestly promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Shusheng took over the Ministry of Rites, Shude was quietly promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 歷太常少卿，南京太僕卿，以右僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, then as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief touring and governing Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, then was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to govern Shandong.

sentences.zh: 樹德素清嚴，約束僚吏，屏絕聲伎。

translations.literal: Shude had always been austere and strict; he restrained his subordinate officials and barred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Shude had always been stern and incorruptible. He kept his staff on a tight rein and banned music and performers.

sentences.zh: 山東民壯改民兵，戍薊門，隆慶末令歲輸銀二萬四千，罷其戍役。

translations.literal: The militia of Shandong had been converted from sturdy commoners and garrisoned Jizhou Pass; at the end of Longqing an order required an annual payment of twenty-four thousand taels of silver and abolished their garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's militia, drawn from sturdy commoners, had garrisoned Jizhou Pass. At the end of Longqing the court ordered them to pay twenty-four thousand taels of silver a year in lieu of service.

sentences.zh: 尋命增輸三萬，樹德請如河南例罷之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an order increased the payment to thirty thousand; Shude asked that it be abolished according to the Henan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the quota was raised to thirty thousand taels. Shude asked that the levy be abolished, following the Henan precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，而為免增輸之數。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, but exempted the increased payment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the abolition but waived the increase.

sentences.zh: 德府白雲湖故民田，為王所奪，後已還民，王復結中官謀復之。

translations.literal: The former civilian fields of Baiyun Lake in the Princedom of De had been seized by the prince; later they had been returned to the people, but the prince again colluded with eunuchs to plot their recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyun Lake in the Princedom of De had once been commoners' farmland until the prince seized it. It had later been returned to the people, but the prince now colluded with eunuchs to take it back.

sentences.zh: 樹德爭不得，乞休歸。

translations.literal: Shude contested the matter without success and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Shude fought the scheme and lost, then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 蕭廩，字可發，萬安人。

translations.literal: Xiao Lin, styled Kefa, was a man of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Lin, courtesy name Kefa, was a native of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖乾元，以御史劾劉瑾，廷杖下獄，終雲南副使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ganyuan, as a censor, impeached Liu Jin, was beaten at court and imprisoned, and ended his career as vice commissioner in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ganyuan had impeached Liu Jin as a censor, was beaten at court and thrown into prison, and ended his career as vice commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 廩舉嘉靖末進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Lin passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Jiajing reign and was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lin earned his jinshi degree at the end of Jiajing and was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年擢御史。

translations.literal: Longqing year three, promoted censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longqing, he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 因地震，請加禮中宮。

translations.literal: Because of an earthquake, he requested increased rites for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: On account of an earthquake, he petitioned that greater honor be shown to the empress.

sentences.zh: 已，出核陜西四鎮兵食。

translations.literal: Thereafter, sent out to audit the military provisions of the four garrisons in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was dispatched to audit the military provisions of the four garrisons in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 斥將吏隱占卒數萬人歸伍。

translations.literal: He exposed officers and officials who had concealed and held soldiers, returning tens of thousands of men to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed military officers and officials who had concealed and misappropriated soldiers, returning tens of thousands of men to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 固原州海剌都之地，密邇松山，為楚府牧地。

translations.literal: The land at Hailadu in Guyuan Prefecture, close to Songshan, was pasture belonging to the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The land at Hailadu in Guyuan Prefecture, close to Songshan, was princely pasture belonging to the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 廩言楚府封武昌，牧地在塞下，與寇接，王所收四五百金，而奸宄窟穴，弊甚大，宜諭使獻之朝廷。

translations.literal: Lin said the Prince of Chu was enfeoffed at Wuchang, yet his pastures lay below the frontier and bordered bandits; the prince collected four or five hundred taels of gold, while bandits made their nests there, causing great harm — he should be instructed to surrender it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued that the Prince of Chu had been enfeoffed at Wuchang, but his pastures lay below the frontier and bordered raiders; the prince collected four or five hundred taels of gold, yet bandits made their nests there, causing great harm — he should be instructed to surrender the land to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 已，改巡茶馬。

translations.literal: Thereafter, he was reassigned as tea-and-horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was reassigned as commissioner for tea and horses.

sentences.zh: 七苑牧地，養馬八千七百餘匹，而占地五萬五千三百頃有奇。

translations.literal: The pastures of the seven stud farms supported more than eight thousand seven hundred horses, yet occupied more than fifty-three thousand three hundred odd qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: The pastures of the seven stud farms supported more than 8,700 horses, yet occupied over 53,300 qing of land.

sentences.zh: 廩但給萬二千二百餘頃，歲益課二萬。

translations.literal: Lin allowed only a little more than twelve thousand two hundred qing, with an annual increase in tax revenue of twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lin allotted only a little more than 12,200 qing, yielding an annual increase in tax revenue of 20,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，巡按浙江。

translations.literal: Wanli year one, touring censor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli, he served as touring censor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 請祀建文朝忠臣十二人，從祀王守仁於文廟。

translations.literal: He requested sacrifice to the twelve loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign, and that Wang Shouren be enshrined in the Confucian temple as an associate sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to sacrifice to the twelve loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign, and to have Wang Shouren enshrined in the Confucian temple as an associate sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尋擢太僕少卿，再遷南京太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred again to Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred again to Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 九年，由光祿卿改右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: Year nine, from Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he was changed to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he moved from Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時方核天下隱田，大吏爭希張居正指增賦，廩令如額而止。

translations.literal: At that time the empire was auditing concealed landholdings; high officials vied to follow Zhang Juzheng's lead in raising taxes, but Lin ordered that assessments stop at the proper quota.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire was auditing concealed landholdings; high officials vied to follow Zhang Juzheng's lead in raising taxes, but Lin ordered that assessments stop at the proper quota.

sentences.zh: 境內回回部常群行拾麥穗，間或草竊，耀州以變告。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction, Hui communities often went about in groups gleaning wheat ears; occasionally they committed petty theft, and Yaozhou reported an outbreak of unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction, Hui communities often went about in groups gleaning wheat ears; occasionally they committed petty theft, and Yaozhou reported an outbreak of unrest.

sentences.zh: 廩撫諭之，戮數人，變遂定；

translations.literal: Lin pacified and instructed them, executed several men, and the unrest was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pacified and instructed them, executed several men, and the unrest was settled;

sentences.zh: 令拾麥毋帶兵器，儕偶不得至十人。

translations.literal: He ordered that gleaners carry no weapons, and that groups not exceed ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that gleaners carry no weapons and that groups not exceed ten persons.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，移撫浙江。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and transferred to Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先以賞貢使，歲增造彩幣二千。

translations.literal: Previously, to reward tribute envoys, annual production of brocade tribute goods had been increased by two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, to reward tribute envoys, annual production of brocade tribute goods had been increased by two thousand pieces.

sentences.zh: 廩請均之福建及徽、寧諸府，從之。

translations.literal: Lin petitioned to spread this evenly among Fujian and the prefectures of Huizhou, Ningguo, and the like; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin petitioned to spread this burden evenly among Fujian and the prefectures of Huizhou, Ningguo, and the like; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 已，請減上供織造，不許。

translations.literal: Thereafter, he petitioned to reduce imperial tribute weaving; this was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he petitioned to reduce imperial tribute weaving; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遷工部右侍郎，召改刑部。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works, summoned and reassigned to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works, then summoned and reassigned to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 進兵部左侍郎，以官卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Left Vice Minister of War; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the title of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Minister.

sentences.zh: 廩初從歐陽德、鄒守益遊。

translations.literal: In his youth Lin had studied under Ouyang De and Zou Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Lin had studied under Ouyang De and Zou Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 制行醇謹，故所至有立。

translations.literal: His conduct was pure and careful, so wherever he served he achieved lasting results.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was pure and careful, so wherever he served he achieved lasting results.

sentences.zh: 賈三近，字德修，嶧縣人。

translations.literal: Jia Sanjin, courtesy name Dexiu, was a native of Yi County.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sanjin, courtesy name Dexiu, was a native of Yi County.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Longqing year two jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，疏言：「善治者守法以宜民，去其太甚而已。

translations.literal: Sixth month of year four, he submitted a memorial saying: 「A ruler who governs well upholds the law to suit the people, removing only what is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, he submitted a memorial saying: 「A ruler who governs well upholds the law to suit the people, removing only what is excessive.

sentences.zh: 今廟堂之令不信於郡縣，郡縣之令不信於小民。

translations.literal: Today the court's orders are not trusted in the prefectures and counties, and the prefectures' and counties' orders are not trusted among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court's orders are not trusted in the prefectures and counties, and the prefectures' and counties' orders are not trusted among the common people.

sentences.zh: 蠲租矣而催科愈急，振濟矣而追逋自如，恤刑矣而冤死相望。

translations.literal: Rent is remitted, yet collection grows only more urgent; relief is extended, yet pursuit of arrears proceeds as before; mercy in punishments is proclaimed, yet wrongful deaths stretch on in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Rent is remitted, yet collection grows only more urgent; relief is extended, yet pursuit of arrears proceeds as before; mercy in punishments is proclaimed, yet wrongful deaths stretch on in sight of one another.

sentences.zh: 正額之輸，上供之需，邊疆之費，雖欲損毫厘不可得。

translations.literal: The regular quotas, the needs of imperial tribute, and frontier expenses — though one wished to reduce them by the slightest measure, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The regular quotas, the needs of imperial tribute, and frontier expenses — though one wished to reduce them by the slightest measure, it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 形格勢制，莫可如何。

translations.literal: Circumstance checks and power constrains; nothing can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstance checked and power constrained; nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 且監司考課，多取振作集事之人，而輕寬平和易之士，守令雖賢，安養之心漸移於苛察，撫字之念日奪於征輸，民安得不困！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the examinations of circuit intendants, those who are forceful and gather achievements are mostly chosen, while men who are lenient, peaceful, and easygoing are slighted; though magistrates be worthy, their hearts for nourishing the people gradually shift toward harsh scrutiny, and their concern for care and comfort is daily seized by tax collection — how can the people not fall into distress!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the examinations of circuit intendants, those who were forceful and gathered achievements were mostly chosen, while men who were lenient, peaceful, and easygoing were slighted; though magistrates were worthy, their hearts for nourishing the people gradually shifted toward harsh scrutiny, and their concern for care and comfort was daily seized by tax collection — how could the people not fall into distress!

sentences.zh: 乞戒有司務守法。

translations.literal: I beg that officials be admonished to uphold the law.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that officials be admonished to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 而監司殿最毋但取旦夕功，失惇大之體。」

translations.literal: And that circuit intendants, in ranking performance, not take only short-term achievements and lose the larger principle of generous governance.」
translations.idiomatic: And that circuit intendants, in ranking performance, not take only short-term achievements and lose the larger principle of generous governance.」

sentences.zh: 已，復疏言：「撫按諸臣遇州縣長吏，率重甲科而輕鄉舉。

translations.literal: Soon after, he again submitted a memorial saying: 「When grand coordinators and touring censors meet with chief magistrates of prefectures and counties, they generally favor jinshi and slight provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he again submitted a memorial saying: 「When grand coordinators and touring censors meet with chief magistrates of prefectures and counties, they generally favor jinshi and slight provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 同一寬也，在進士則為撫字，在舉人則為姑息。

translations.literal: The same leniency, in a jinshi, is called care for the people; in a provincial graduate, indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The same leniency, in a jinshi, was called care for the people; in a provincial graduate, indulgence.

sentences.zh: 同一嚴也，在進士則為精明，在舉人則為苛戾。

translations.literal: The same strictness, in a jinshi, is called shrewdness; in a provincial graduate, cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The same strictness, in a jinshi, was called shrewdness; in a provincial graduate, cruelty.

sentences.zh: 是以為舉人者，非華顛豁齒不就選；
