translations.literal: When Xiangchun reached Henan and a conference had just convened, clansmen of the Zhou princely house suspected that Tie's memorial reflected the intent of the clan elder Mu Xian, and they mobbed and beat Mu Xian nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun had barely reached Henan and begun deliberations when Zhou-house kinsmen, suspecting Tie's memorial came from clan steward Mu Xian, attacked Mu Xian in a crowd and nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 象春以狀聞，帝為奪諸人歲祿。

translations.literal: Xiangchun reported the facts, and the emperor stripped those men of their annual stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun reported what had happened, and the emperor confiscated the offenders' yearly stipends.

sentences.zh: 象春復以次詣秦、晉諸藩，奏上便宜十五事，多著為令。

translations.literal: Xiangchun next proceeded in order to the Qin and Jin princely establishments, memorializing fifteen expedient measures, many of which were enacted as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured the Qin and Jin establishments in turn, submitting fifteen practical proposals, most of which became standing rules.

sentences.zh: 真人張國祥乞三年一覲，象春言左道無民社寄，不當在述職之列。

translations.literal: The Daoist master Zhang Guoxiang asked to attend court audience once every three years; Xiangchun said heterodox teachings had no charge over the people or the altars of soil and grain and should not be in the ranks of those reporting for duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoist adept Zhang Guoxiang petitioned for triennial audiences, Xiangchun argued that occult sects bore no responsibility for the realm and ought not to be counted among officials presenting themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 時詔許後父永年伯王偉乘肩輿，象春言：「勛戚不乘輿，祖制也。

translations.literal: At the time an edict permitted the empress's father, Yongnian Earl Wang Wei, to ride in a sedan chair; Xiangchun said: "Meritorious kinsmen do not ride sedan chairs—this is ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed the empress's father, Yongnian Earl Wang Wei, to use a shoulder sedan; Xiangchun protested: "Imperial in-laws do not ride sedans—that is ancestral law.

sentences.zh: 固安伯陳景行、武清伯李偉，太后父，衰白封，始賜肩輿。

translations.literal: Gu'an Earl Chen Jingxing and Wuqing Earl Li Wei, fathers of empresses dowager, were enfeoffed in old age with white hair and only then granted sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu'an Earl Chen Jingxing and Wuqing Earl Li Wei, both fathers of empresses dowager, received their enfeoffments in their gray-haired years and only then were given the sedan privilege.

sentences.zh: 定國公徐文璧班首重臣，嗣爵久，故亦蒙殊典。

translations.literal: Duke of Dingguo Xu Wenbi was the foremost senior minister; he had long held his title in succession, and therefore also received this special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo Duke Xu Wenbi, the ranking grandee, had held his hereditary title for many years and so likewise received that exceptional grant.

sentences.zh: 今偉非三人比，乞寢前命。」

translations.literal: Now Wei is not comparable to those three men; I beg that the previous order be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: Wei cannot be compared with those three; I ask that the earlier command be revoked."

sentences.zh: 皆不許。

translations.literal: None was granted.
translations.idiomatic: None of these pleas was accepted.

sentences.zh: 孟秋將享廟，帝齋宿宮中，象春言當在便殿，不當於內寢。

translations.literal: In mid-autumn, when the emperor was to offer at the ancestral temple, he kept ritual abstinence within the palace; Xiangchun said he should be in the side hall, not in the inner sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared for the autumn temple sacrifice and kept vigil in the palace, Xiangchun insisted he should observe abstinence in the audience hall, not in the private inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，停俸三月。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and suspended his salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and withheld his salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 已，因災異，言：「外吏貪殘不當遣緹騎逮問，宮禁邃密不當宿重兵，廷臣建言貶黜當敘遷，內臣有犯當付外廷按治。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward, citing calamities and anomalies, he said: "Greedy and cruel outer officials ought not to be seized by the imperial guard for interrogation; the inner palace, being deep and secluded, ought not to quarter heavy troops; court officials whose advice leads to demotion ought to be promoted in due course; and inner eunuchs who commit offenses ought to be handed to the outer court for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, invoking omens and disasters, he argued that rapacious local officials should not be hauled in by the emperor's mounted guards, that the secluded inner quarters should not house large garrisons, that censured remonstrators deserved eventual reinstatement, and that offending palace eunuchs should be tried by the civil administration.

sentences.zh: 帝報聞。

translations.literal: The emperor acknowledged the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 象春在諫垣久，前後七十餘疏，多關軍國計。

translations.literal: Xiangchun had long served in the remonstrance offices and submitted more than seventy memorials in all, many bearing on military and state policy.
translations.idiomatic: Having spent years in the censorial and remonstrance posts, he filed over seventy memorials, most touching on military and fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 請復建文年號，加景帝廟謚，尤為時所稱。

translations.literal: His requests to restore the Jianwen reign title and to add a temple epithet for the Jing Emperor were especially praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His calls to revive the Jianwen reign name and augment the temple title of the Jing Emperor won particular acclaim.

sentences.zh: 出為山東參政。

translations.literal: He went out as administration vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as administration vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 妖賊郭大通為亂，計擒之。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Guo Datong raised a disturbance, and he devised a plan to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer-bandit Guo Datong rebelled, he engineered his capture.

sentences.zh: 歷山西左布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Left Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Left Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以右副都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 倭躪朝鮮，濱海郡邑悉戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Japanese raiders trampled Korea, all coastal prefectures and districts were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: As Japanese forces ravaged Korea, every maritime command went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 象春拊軍民，供饋運，應機立辦。

translations.literal: Xiangchun comforted troops and civilians, supplied transport, and handled emergencies as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun reassured soldiers and populace, organized supplies and transport, and met each crisis as it came.

sentences.zh: 中使陳增以礦稅至，象春疏論其害。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Chen Zeng arrived to levy mining taxes; Xiangchun memorialized on the harm they caused.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuch tax commissioner Chen Zeng came to impose mining levies, Xiangchun memorialized against the damage.

sentences.zh: 福山知縣韋國賢忤增被侵辱，象春力保持之，增遂劾國賢沮撓，象春黨庇。

translations.literal: Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian offended Zeng and was insulted and abused; Xiangchun strove to protect him, whereupon Zeng impeached Guoxian for obstruction and Xiangchun for shielding a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Fushan magistrate Wei Guoxian crossed Chen Zeng and was publicly humiliated; Xiangchun fought to shield him, and Zeng retaliated by charging Guoxian with interference and Xiangchun with favoritism.

sentences.zh: 詔逮國賢，奪象春俸，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guoxian arrested and Xiangchun's salary seized; he then cited illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Guoxian seized and docked Xiangchun's pay; Xiangchun thereupon resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起南京工部右侍郎，未上卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing yet died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鐘化民，字維新，仁和人。

translations.literal: Zhong Huamin, courtesy name Weixin, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Huamin, style name Weixin, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 萬曆八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授惠安知縣，多異政。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Huian and produced many outstanding policies.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Huian he carried out numerous notable reforms.

sentences.zh: 御史安九域薦於朝，以俸未及期，移知樂平，治復最。

translations.literal: Censor An Jiucheng recommended him at court, but because his salary term had not expired he was transferred to magistrate of Leping, where his governance again ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Censor An Jiucheng recommended him to the court; still within his salary term, he was moved to Leping, where his administration again topped the evaluations.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 與同官何卓、王慎德交章請建儲，不報。

translations.literal: Together with colleagues He Zhuo and Wang Shende he jointly memorialized to establish the heir apparent; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He joined censors He Zhuo and Wang Shende in successive memorials demanding the crown prince's installation, all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 出視陜西茶馬，言：「邊塞土寒，獨畜馬為業。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Shaanxi horse-tea administration, he said: "On the frontier the soil is cold and raising horses is the sole livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Shaanxi's tea-for-horses trade, he wrote: "Border lands are frigid, and horse breeding is the people's chief livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今慮其闌出為厲禁，於是民間孳息與境內貿易俱廢，公私緩急亦無所資。

translations.literal: Now, fearing that horses would slip across the border and become a scourge, strict bans were imposed, so that household breeding and trade within the territory were both abolished, and neither public nor private needs could be met in urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing animals would cross the frontier and cause trouble, officials banned everything, ending domestic breeding and internal trade alike so that neither state nor household could meet sudden needs.

sentences.zh: 請聽逾境販鬻，特不得入番中。

translations.literal: I ask that cross-border sale be permitted, only that they must not enter the fan territories.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that cross-border sales be allowed, provided horses did not enter the tribal interior.

sentences.zh: 又曩寧夏乏餉，歲發萬金易米二萬七千石，後所司幹沒，濫征之民。

translations.literal: Moreover, formerly when Ningxia lacked funds, ten thousand taels of gold were issued each year to buy twenty-seven thousand piculs of rice; afterward the responsible officials embezzled it and levied the people indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that when Ningxia ran short of funds, the court once sent ten thousand taels yearly to buy twenty-seven thousand piculs of grain, but officials later skimmed the money and extorted the populace.

sentences.zh: 請以墾田粟補之，永停征派。」

translations.literal: I ask that reclaimed-field grain make up the shortfall and that the levy be stopped permanently."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed covering the gap with grain from reclaimed fields and abolishing the exaction forever."

sentences.zh: 俱報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 巡按山東，歲旱，請蠲振先發後聞。

translations.literal: While touring as investigating censor in Shandong, in a year of drought he requested tax relief and relief grain be disbursed first and reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: On drought duty in Shandong he urged that tax remissions and famine relief be issued immediately and reported to the throne afterward.

sentences.zh: 坐寧夏時取官銀交際，為尚寶丞周弘禴所劾，調行人司正。

translations.literal: Because while in Ningxia he had taken official silver for social exchanges, he was impeached by Court of Imperial Seals director Zhou Hongfu and demoted to director of the Bureau of Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He was accused by Court of Imperial Seals director Zhou Hongfu of using official silver for gifts while in Ningxia and was transferred to director of the Bureau of Envoys.

sentences.zh: 累遷儀制郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to director in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 沈王呈堯由支庶嗣，請封其庶子為郡王，化民持不可。

translations.literal: Prince Shen Yaochun, a collateral heir, succeeded to the title and asked that his son by a concubine be enfeoffed as a commandery prince; Huamin maintained this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shen of Yao, a cadet line successor, sought to ennoble a concubine-born son as a commandery prince, Huamin objected.

sentences.zh: 帝傳諭曰：「第予虛名，令藉是婚娶耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent word: "Just grant an empty title so he may marry by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied privately: "Give only an empty title so he can marry on that basis.

sentences.zh: 化民奏曰：「沈王子與元子孰親？

translations.literal: Huamin memorialized: "Between the prince's son and the primary son, which is closer?
translations.idiomatic: Huamin rejoined: "Which is nearer kin—the prince's younger son or the heir apparent?

sentences.zh: 王子不即封，慮妨婚娶，元子不即立，不慮妨豫教乎？」

translations.literal: If the prince's son is not enfeoffed for fear of hindering marriage, is the primary son not established for fear of hindering early instruction?
translations.idiomatic: If you withhold enfeoffment from the younger son lest marriage suffer, will you likewise delay installing the heir lest his tutoring suffer?

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以化民辭直，無以難。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, but because Huamin's words were blunt he had no way to refute them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fumed, yet Huamin's blunt logic left him no good reply.

sentences.zh: 帝命並封三王，化民與顧允成等面詰王錫爵於朝房。

translations.literal: When the emperor ordered simultaneous enfeoffment of three princes, Huamin with Gu Yuncheng and others confronted Wang Xinjue in the court anteroom.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne commanded enfeoffing three princes at once, Huamin and Gu Yuncheng openly challenged Wang Xinjue in the ministers' waiting room.

sentences.zh: 尋進光祿丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，河南大饑，人相食，命化民兼河南道御史往振。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Henan suffered great famine and people ate one another; he was ordered as Henan-route censor on concurrent duty to bring relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, when Henan starved so badly that men devoured one another, he was sent as concurrent Henan-route censor to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 荒政具舉，民大悅。

translations.literal: He carried out famine policies comprehensively, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He implemented every measure of famine relief, to the people's deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 既竣，繪圖以進。

translations.literal: When finished, he painted pictures and presented them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On completing the mission he submitted illustrated reports to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，褒諭者再。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and commended him twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lauded his work with repeated commendations.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以右僉都御史巡撫河南，討平南陽礦盜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan and suppressed the Nanyang mining bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan, crushing the Nanyang mining rebels.

sentences.zh: 夾河賊嘯聚數千人，復督兵破之。

translations.literal: Bandits along the Jia River gathered in cries numbering several thousand men; he again directed troops and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand brigands rallied along the Jia River, and he once more led troops to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 時方采礦，抗疏力諫。

translations.literal: At the time mining was being carried out; he submitted a forceful memorial in protest.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial mining expanded, he filed a vigorous memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 化民短小精悍，多智計。

translations.literal: Huamin was short in stature, keen and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Huamin was small in build but sharp and full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 居官勤厲，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Diligent in office wherever he served, he won renown everywhere he went.
translations.idiomatic: He worked tirelessly in every post and left a reputation at each.

sentences.zh: 遍歷八府，延父老問疾苦。

translations.literal: He passed through all eight prefectures and summoned elders to ask their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Touring all eight prefectures, he called elders before him to hear their grievances.

sentences.zh: 勞瘁卒官，士民相率頌於朝。

translations.literal: Worn out by labor he died in office, and officials and people together praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted by overwork he died in service, and gentry and commoners alike sang his praises at the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔贈右副都御史，賜祠曰忠惠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and granted a shrine entitled Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously made him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and dedicated a shrine named Zhonghui.

sentences.zh: 吳達可，字安節，宜興人，尚書儼從孫也。

translations.literal: Wu Dake, courtesy name Anjie, was a native of Yixing and a great-nephew of Minister Wu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dake, style name Anjie, came from Yixing and was a grand-nephew of Minister Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知會稽、上高、豐城，並有聲。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Kuaiji, Shanggao, and Fengcheng, winning reputation at each.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Kuaiji, Shanggao, and Fengcheng in turn, earning praise in each post.

sentences.zh: 選授御史。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen and appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏請御經筵勤學，時與大臣臺諫面議政務，報聞。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the emperor attend the classics lectures and study diligently, and that he meet regularly with grand ministers and censors to discuss state affairs; the court acknowledged it.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to keep up the classics lectures, study diligently, and confer face to face with ministers and remonstrators on policy; the memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯久疾乞休，未得請。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao had long been ill and begged to retire but had not received permission.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao, long ill, had sought retirement without success.

sentences.zh: 達可力言志臯衰庸，宜罷，不納。

translations.literal: Dake forcefully said Zhigao was decrepit and mediocre and ought to be dismissed; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Dake bluntly argued that Zhigao was senile and incompetent and should go; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，請因始和布令，舉皇長子冊立冠婚禮，簡輔臣補臺諫，撤礦稅中使，不報。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he asked that, with the year's harmony newly begun, edicts be issued to perform the crown prince's investiture, capping, and wedding rites, to appoint supporting ministers and fill censorial posts, and to withdraw mining-tax eunuchs; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he petitioned that, as spring began, the throne proclaim the heir's investiture, capping, and marriage, replenish ministers and censors, and recall mining-tax eunuchs—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 視鹽長蘆。

translations.literal: He was sent to inspect the Changlu salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to inspect the Changlu salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 歲侵，繪上饑民十四圖，力請振貸。

translations.literal: When the year suffered invasion, he painted and submitted fourteen pictures of starving people and forcefully requested relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he presented fourteen sketches of starving folk and pressed for relief grain and loans.

sentences.zh: 稅使馬堂、張日華議加鹽稅，奸商妄稱嘉靖中大同用兵貸其貲三萬六千金，請於鹽課補給，戶部許之。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners Ma Tang and Zhang Rihua proposed raising the salt tax; unscrupulous merchants falsely claimed that in the Jiajing era the Datong campaign had borrowed thirty-six thousand seven hundred jin of their funds and asked repayment from salt levies, and the Ministry of Revenue consented.
translations.idiomatic: Tax agents Ma Tang and Zhang Rihua sought higher salt duties while conniving merchants claimed the Jiajing Datong war had borrowed 36,700 jin from them and demanded repayment from salt revenues, which the Ministry of Revenue approved.

sentences.zh: 達可皆抗爭，事得已。

translations.literal: Dake resisted all of these, and the matters were dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Dake fought each proposal and saw them shelved.

sentences.zh: 改按江西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as touring censor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 稅使潘相毆折輔國將軍謀圮肢，並系宗人宗達，誣以劫課，劾上饒知縣李鴻主使。

translations.literal: Tax commissioner Pan Xiang beat and broke the bones of the defender-general Mou Ji, and also imprisoned the clansman Zong Da, falsely charging him with robbing tax goods and impeaching Shangrao magistrate Li Hong as the instigator.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Pan Xiang assaulted defender-general Mou Ji until his limbs were broken, jailed kinsman Zong Da on a trumped-up charge of robbing tax goods, and impeached Shangrao magistrate Li Hong as mastermind.

sentences.zh: 帝切責謀圮等，奪鴻官。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked Mou Ji and others and stripped Hong of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply censured Mou Ji and his party and dismissed Hong from office.

sentences.zh: 達可言：「宗人無故受刑，又重之以詰責，將使天潢人人自危。

translations.literal: Dake said: "Clansmen were punished without cause and were further subjected to stern rebuke; this will make everyone of the imperial lineage feel insecure.
translations.idiomatic: Dake protested: "Imperial kinsmen were beaten without cause and then scolded again—every branch of the house will live in fear.

sentences.zh: 鴻無辜，不當黜。

translations.literal: Hong is innocent and ought not to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong is guiltless and should not be removed.

sentences.zh: 願亟正相罪，復鴻官。」

translations.literal: I beg that Xiang's crime be corrected at once and Hong's office restored.
translations.idiomatic: I urge immediate punishment of Pan Xiang and reinstatement of Hong.

sentences.zh: 同官湯兆京亦極論相罪，且言遼東高淮、陜西梁永、山東陳增、廣東李鳳、雲南楊榮皆元惡，為民害，不可一日留。

translations.literal: His colleague Tang Zhaojing also argued Xiang's guilt at length and said that Gao Huai of Liaodong, Liang Yong of Shaanxi, Chen Zeng of Shandong, Li Feng of Guangdong, and Yang Rong of Yunnan were all arch-villains harming the people and could not be kept a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Colleague Tang Zhaojing likewise denounced Pan Xiang and named Liaodong's Gao Huai, Shaanxi's Liang Yong, Shandong's Chen Zeng, Guangdong's Li Feng, and Yunnan's Yang Rong as chief evils who must not remain another day.

sentences.zh: 皆弗聽。

translations.literal: None was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 鴻，吳人，大學士申時行之婿。

translations.literal: Hong was a man of Wu and son-in-law of Grand Secretary Shen Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, a native of Wu, was married to Grand Secretary Shen Shixing's daughter.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年舉北闈鄉試，為吏部郎中高桂所攻。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Wanli he passed the northern metropolitan examination at the provincial level and was attacked by Ministry of Personnel director Gao Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli sixteen he passed the northern provincial examination and was assailed by Personnel director Gao Gui.

sentences.zh: 後七年成進士。

translations.literal: Seven years later he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years on he finally attained his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 至是，抗相，以強直稱。

translations.literal: Now, resisting Xiang, he was famed for his firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: By defying Pan Xiang here he won renown for unyielding integrity.

sentences.zh: 相又請開廣信銅塘山，采取大木，鑿泰和斌姥山石膏，達可復極諫不可，閣臣亦爭之，乃寢。

translations.literal: Xiang also asked to open the Guangxin Tongtang Mountain to fell great timber and to quarry gypsum at Taihe Binlaoshan; Dake again remonstrated forcefully that this could not be done, and grand secretaries also contended; the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xiang further sought to open Guangxin's Tongtang Mountain for timber and Taihe's Binlaoshan for gypsum; Dake again protested vehemently, cabinet ministers joined him, and the projects were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 還掌河南道事。

translations.literal: On returning he took charge of Henan-route affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he resumed duties on the Henan route.

sentences.zh: 佐溫純大計京官。

translations.literal: He assisted Wen Chun in the grand evaluation of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: He aided Wen Chun in the major review of metropolitan officials.

sentences.zh: 尋陳新政要機，痛規首輔沈一貫。

translations.literal: Soon he set forth essentials of the new administration and sharply admonished chief grand secretary Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon laid out priorities for the new reign and sharply criticized chief minister Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 疏留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was retained in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That memorial was held within the palace and never acted on.

sentences.zh: 擢太僕少卿，再遷南京太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and again promoted to Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, then to Nanjing Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 召改光祿，進通政使。

translations.literal: He was summoned and transferred to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then advanced to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he moved to the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫史晉以罪罷，妄投封章詆朝貴。

translations.literal: The brocade-guard colonel Shi Jin was dismissed for crime and rashly submitted a sealed memorial slandering court dignitaries.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade Guard colonel Shi Jin, dismissed for misconduct, recklessly filed a sealed memorial defaming high officials.

sentences.zh: 達可封其疏而劾之，晉尋得罪。

translations.literal: Dake sealed the memorial and impeached him; Jin soon fell into guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Dake kept the document sealed and impeached him; Jin was soon found guilty.

sentences.zh: 奏請正疏式、屏讒邪、重駁正、懲奸宄數事，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to standardize memorial format, bar slander, weight rejection of errors, and punish treacherous villains in several matters; the emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He requested proper memorial forms, silencing calumny, honoring rebuttals, and punishing wicked plotters—measures the emperor commended and adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏乞休去。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he asked leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右副都御史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After he died he was posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：龐尚鵬諸人歷官中外，才諝幹局，咸有可稱。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Pang Shangpeng and the others served inside and outside the court; in talent, shrewdness, and practical capacity they all had merits worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Pang Shangpeng and his fellows served at court and in the provinces; in ability, shrewdness, and executive skill each had something to his credit.

sentences.zh: 賈三近陳時政，多長者之言，其言資格，深中積弊。

translations.literal: Jia Sanjin on current policy spoke many words of an elder's wisdom; his talk on seniority deeply hit accumulated abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sanjin's counsel on current affairs often sounded the seasoned voice of an elder statesman, and his argument about seniority struck at deep-seated abuses.

sentences.zh: 謝傑卻屬吏饋，亦無愧楊震云。

translations.literal: Xie Jie refused gifts from subordinate officials and likewise had no shame before Yang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie too refused presents from subordinates, no less honorably than Yang Zhen.
